attacks.claim: Each booking now holds a pooled connection for the whole transaction, including time spent queued on the per-class row lock. A hot class can occupy the shared pool, which contradicts the claim that the change does not affect other classes. The pool size and checkout timeout are not stated, and the 5s statement_timeout also covers lock waits.
attacks.evidence: serializes bookings per class without affecting other classes; The pg pool sets statement_timeout=5s; ABSENT: pool max size, connectionTimeoutMillis, and any load test at launch-spike volume

attacks.claim: No issue under this lens. No schema change is made, so reverting is a code revert.

The UUID regex requires the hyphenated 8-4-4-4-12 form, so Postgres-accepted inputs without hyphens, which previously reached the query, now return 404. This is a silent behaviour change not mentioned in the PR. The closed check also runs before the existing-booking check, so a member who already holds a booking gets 409 once the class starts rather than 200.

The oversell problem rests on anecdotal support reports with no reproduction or before/after measurement. The concurrency test uses Promise.all over a pool, so it may not reliably produce interleaving that exposes the old race.
attacks.evidence: support saw classes oversold by 1-2; ABSENT: a test that fails on the pre-change code
